material_definitions: The Li+ superionic argyrodites Li6PS5-xSexBr (0 <= x <= 1) have been synthesized to study the influence of increasing anion polarizability and selenium substitution.
The replacement of sulfur with larger and more polarizable selenium affects lattice dynamics and expands the unit cell volume linearly following Vegard's law.
Site disorder between Br- and Ch2- sites was found to decrease with increasing Se content, which influences the intercage jump distances for Li+ ions.
Structural characterization was performed using Rietveld refinement of powder XRD and neutron pair distribution function analysis to resolve Li+ occupancy and anion disorder.
Samples exhibit minor impurity phase fractions of LiBr and Li3OBr (<5 wt %), which are unlikely to significantly affect ionic transport.
